title: 3D Render
description: 3D render, the 3d render look, is a person as product visualization: clean global illumination, shader skin slightly too perfect, infinite cyc, contact shadows that never dirty. They should look computed, and photochemical grain is a joke if you add it.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Fashion that wants to be a toy, ads, a character who is not quite flesh: studio HDRI, turntable still, no film grain unless you are hybridizing on purpose. A period drama usually dies here.
The library cousin is motion capture into an invented body, where attention and hesitation matter more than spectacle. The named look on the page is the computed surface.
Do not confuse a photograph labeled CGI with this. If pores and grain survive, you still shot a camera.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lock a studio camera, 50mm to 85mm, eye height or a slight turntable three-quarter. HDRI wrap, subsurface that is slightly too even, infinite cyc, perfect contacts.
No grain, no dirty anamorphic. Prompt: 3D-render look of [Subject], CG shader, clean GI, a person as a product visualization.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Kill the grain, wrap the light. 3D-render look of [Subject], CG shader, clean GI, a person as a product visualization.
Add studio HDRI, infinite cyc, too-perfect subsurface, turntable still, no film grain, no dirty flare.

A small fictional creature receives a repaired toy from a human friend. Preserve a specific performance: guarded gaze, delayed recognition, relaxed shoulders and a tentative reach. Stable character model, precise finger contact and matched eye level. Use performance reference and animation rather than relying on a generic happy expression.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: A photograph with CGI in the prompt that still has pores and grain, or a slide into Photogrammetry dirt. The tell is photochemical noise.
Fix it: shader wrap, clean GI, cyc, computed skin.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is 3D Render in film?
A computed-surface look: clean GI, shader skin, product-visualization light on a person. Related pipelines include motion capture into an invented body, which still needs animation judgment.
3D Render vs Photogrammetry
Photogrammetry captures real surfaces, including dirt. 3D render is shader and GI, too clean on purpose. If you can see scanned grime, you wanted photogrammetry.
When should I use 3D Render?
Ads, toy-fashion, a character who is not quite flesh. Skip period realism unless the computation is the point.
How do I prompt 3D Render for AI image or video?
Studio HDRI, no grain, then: 3D-render look of [Subject], CG shader, clean GI, a person as a product visualization. Demand infinite cyc and too-perfect skin.
